reconcile.note: Clarke treats Ahaz's exclusion from the royal tombs in Chronicles as a mark of disgrace layered onto Kings' burial notice, not a conflicting report.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen reads Chronicles' burial notice for Ahaz as the people's own censure of a wicked king, layered onto Kings against its own witness.

quotes.text: marks its censure of these wicked kings by withholding from them, or impairing, the honour of royal burial (xxi. 19, 20, xxviii. 27, xxxiii. 10),--in spite of 2Kings ix. 28, xvi. 20, xxi. 1 8.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885 Eng. transl.), on 2 Kings 16:20 and 2 Chronicles 28:27.

sides.snippet: Ahaz slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David: and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.
sides.verseText: Ahaz slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David: and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.

sides.snippet: Ahaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city, even in Jerusalem; for they didn't bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel: and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.
